output.brief:
What is going on: the rise in VA-220 failures is mainly Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not the installers or firmware. The teardown shows seat leakage with the slide seal unseated on 38 of 41 returned valves. Warehouse helium retests found leaks in 11% of 2026 Pellacott valves, versus 1% of 2025 and 0% of Durrant-Hale. Claim rates are similar across legacy and new installers and firmware 4.1 and 4.2, which rules those out. The leak-test certificates also look unreliable: rig LT-04 has been out of service since January, no VA-220 test program runs on the other rigs, and 31 certificate tables repeat four value sequences. Confidence is good on the valve defect and the certificate problem; the seal cause is not yet isolated.

Next: do not release the six held lots on new certificates. Quarantine 2026 Pellacott VA-220 stock, suspend its dock-to-stock status, and release only after Brenmoor runs its own helium leak tests. Pause the installer remediation and firmware blame. Check whether other SupplierPath suppliers' records are similarly unverified. Change scoring to credit only witnessed or rig-logged tests. Investigate the Corlin seal and Line 3 separately.
